From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Draft: Oasis crypto operational playbook + artifacts (internal)

Team — attaching the first draft (oasis_crypto_response_draft.pdf) to the Drive folder. Highlights included in the draft: 

1) BYOK import flow:
- Customer uploads an encrypted key bundle to Redwood Control Plane via a secure, signed upload endpoint.
- Optional remote attestation step when using customer HSMs (PKCS#11 or AWS CloudHSM).
- Import is validated, wrapped using our per-tenant wrapping key held in a FIPS-validated HSM (Luna / Thales / Gemalto compatible).
- Audit trail entries generated for import, key activation, and deletion; entries include actor, timestamp, and operation-id.

2) HSM compatibility & escrow:
- We support Common HSM vendors (Thales, SafeNet/Luna, AWS CloudHSM). Customers can supply their own key material or request generation inside the HSM.
- Key escrow: we provide an optional escrow workflow; keys held in escrow are encrypted under a multi-party KMS key with separation of duties.

3) Key rotation & emergency rotation procedures:
- Routine rotations: configurable per-tenant policy (default 90 days) with automated staging, cutover, and verification. Rotation produces a new key version and rotates wrapped keys across services with zero-downtime rollout using prefix caching and KV cache warmup.
- Emergency rotation: documented runbook — trigger path (security on-call / customer request), immediate revoke & replace, and compatibility fallback to prior model artifact for 48 hours. All emergency rotations generate high-priority audit events and an incident ticket.

4) TLS profile:
- Endpoints require TLS 1.2+; preferred TLS 1.3. We currently advertise and support the following cipher suites: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 for legacy TLS 1.2 compat.
- Mutual TLS available for private deployments and Dedicated pools; mTLS uses customer-provided cert chain or Redwood-managed CA for hosted endpoints.

5) Access controls & separation of duties:
- KMS admin roles (Key Admin, Key Operator, Auditor) with RBAC enforced via our IAM layer and integration with customer IdP (SAML/OIDC).
- No single operator can both import customer keys and approve release to production without a second approver.

6) Evidence artifacts included:
- Redacted KMS audit log sample (kms_audit_log_sample.csv)
- TLS cipher matrix (in PDF)
- Operational playbook PDF (draft)

Notes / Open items for Legal review:
- Redaction level for audit logs (currently removed IPs and request IDs; leaving timestamps and operation-names).
- Whether a BAA addendum is necessary for log-sharing.

Attaching: oasis_crypto_response_draft.pdf (Drive). I'll also upload the CSV sample and mark redaction placeholders.

-Marcus
